card: Validates feerate bucket definitions loaded from fee estimates files on disk during startup. A corrupted estimates file lacking an infinite terminating bucket can cause feerate lookups to read past the end of the internal bucket map. The change throws an error if buckets are non-positive, non-increasing, NaN, or do not end with the infinite feerate sentinel, and adds unit tests mutating saved estimates files. Evidence rests on the author's analysis from an LLM-assisted code audit.
changed_since_previous: Diff and unit tests are now provided; the implementation matches what was described previously.
evidence: Author states: "A block_policy_estimates.dat whose bucket list lacks the infinite last bucket makes a later feerate lookup read past the end of the bucket map. The estimator relies on the last bucket being infinite, so that every feerate finds a bucket." (PR description and commit message)
No external issue or independent reviewer confirmation is cited; the author notes this was identified in an LLM-assisted audit.
problem: If a fee estimates file on disk is corrupted or tampered with such that it lacks the infinite terminal bucket or contains non-monotonic boundaries, feerate lookups can access elements past the end of the bucket map or fail to find a bucket for high feerates.

risk.why: A false positive validation failure would cause the node to treat the fee estimates file as corrupt on startup, discarding cached fee history and resetting estimator state.

summary: Validates the feerate buckets deserialized from fee estimates data files during startup. It checks that the bucket boundaries start positive, increase strictly monotonically without NaN values, and end with the infinite feerate sentinel, throwing a corrupt estimates error if any condition fails. A unit test exercises deserialization rejection on mutated bucket data.
